μνημονεύσας γὰρ τοῦ ἐκ ῥίζης Ἰεσσαὶ ἐπήγαγεν· καὶ πατάξει τὴν γῆν τῷ λόγῳ τοῦ

στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν πνεύματι διὰ χειλέων ἀνελεῖ τὸν ἀσεβῆ. τὸ δὲ πατάξειν
αὐτὸν τὴν γῆν προεῖπε καὶ διὰ τοῦ ὑστέρου τῶν προφητῶν εἰρηκώς· ἀνατελεῖ ὑμῖν
τοῖς φοβουμένοις ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης, καὶ ἴασις ἐν ταῖς πτέρυξιν αὐτοῦ. καὶ μετ'
ὀλίγα· ἰδοὺ ἀποστελῶ ὑμῖν Ἡλίαν τὸν Θεσβίτην, καὶ ἐπήγαγε· μὴ ἐλθὼν πατάξω τὴν
γῆν ἄρδην. Καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ. ἡ ζωὴ ἡμῶν ἐστιν ὁ
Χριστός· ὅταν οὖν ὁ Χριστὸς φανερωθῇ, ἡ ζωὴ ἡμῶν, ἐξ ἀνάγκης καταργεῖ καὶ τὸν
τοῦ θανάτου πρόξενον τὸν διάβολον. κατὰ μίμησιν δὲ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἔρχεται ὁ
σατανᾶς ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ ὁλοκλήρῳ, οὗ ἐστιν ἡ παρου336 σία κατ' ἐνέργειαν τοῦ σατανᾶ
πάσῃ δυνάμει, σημείοις καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. κατὰ μίμησιν τῆς σωματικῆς ἐπιδημίας τοῦ·

ζωῆς οὖν οὐρανόθεν φανερουμένης ἀδύνατον μὴ καταργηθῆναι τὸν τοῦ θανάτου
πρόξενον, οὗ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία κατ' ἐνέργειαν τοῦ σατανᾶ. 336,ξολ2 τοῦτο ὤφειλεν
πεῖσαι τοὺς Ἀπολιναρίδας καὶ τοὺς Ἀριανούς, ὅτι ὅλον ἄνθρωπον ἀνέλαβεν ὁ θεὸς
λόγος. κατὰ γὰρ μίμησιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ τῆς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν οἰκονομίας ἔρχεται ὁ
σατανᾶς καὶ ἐνεργήσει ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ.
thought_title: The breath of Christ's mouth destroys the lawless one
orientation: Severian is explaining 2 Thessalonians 2:8b, showing from Isaiah and Malachi that Christ will strike the earth and destroy the impious one, and that the devil's counterfeit coming in a complete man will be abolished by Christ's appearing.
pass_a_gloss: This also Isaiah, having taken it up beforehand, said: for having remembered the one from the root of Jesse, he added: and he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one. And the striking of the earth by him he foretold also through the last of the prophets, having said: a sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear, and healing in his wings. And after a little: behold, I will send to you Elijah the Tishbite, and he added: lest coming I strike the earth utterly. And he will abolish by the appearing of his coming. Our life is Christ; therefore when Christ is manifested, our life, of necessity he abolishes also the one who procures death, the devil. And in imitation of the Savior the Satan comes in a complete man, whose coming is according to the working of Satan with all power, signs and the rest. In imitation of the bodily sojourn of Christ, of the dispensation for us, the Satan comes, and works in a man, just as I also already said. This is the 'and with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one,' which Isaiah says: for having remembered the one from the root of Jesse, he added: and he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one. And the striking of the earth he foretold also through the last of the prophets: for having said: a sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear me, and after a little: behold, I send to you Elijah the Tishbite, as a final word he added the 'lest coming I strike the earth utterly.' And he will abolish by the appearing of his coming. Life of us the apostle said Christ is, and he added: when your life is manifested. Therefore when life is manifested from heaven, it is impossible that the one who procures death not be abolished, whose coming is according to the working of Satan. This ought to persuade the Apollinarians and the Arians, that the whole man God the Word assumed. For in imitation of the righteousness and of the dispensation for us the Satan comes and will work in a man.

choices.english: with the word of his mouth
choices.why: Literal rendering of the instrumental dative, preserving the Isaiah wording as quoted.
rejected: by the word of his mouth
with the breath of his lips

choices.why: Keeps the two prepositional phrases distinct and literal, matching the source's double expression.
rejected: by the spirit of his lips
with the breath of his lips

choices.why: Adverbial sense of complete destruction, preserving the force of the Malachi quotation.
Literal rendering of πρόξενος as agent who brings about death, keeping the devil's role explicit.
Preserves the repeated phrase as a key structural marker in Severian's argument about counterfeit incarnation.
Literal rendering of ὁλόκληρος as complete or whole, which is central to the anti-Apollinarian point.

pass_b_english: Isaiah also said this beforehand. For after mentioning the one from the root of Jesse, he added: "He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one" (Isaiah 11:4). And he foretold that he would strike the earth also through the last of the prophets, who said: "A sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear me, and healing in its wings" (Malachi 4:2). And after a little: "Behold, I will send you Elijah the Tishbite," and he added: "lest I come and strike the earth utterly" (Malachi 4:5-6). "And he will abolish him by the appearing of his coming" (2 Thessalonians 2:8). Christ is our life. Therefore when Christ, our life, is revealed, of necessity he also abolishes the devil, the one who procures death. Satan comes in imitation of the Savior, in a complete man, whose coming is "according to the working of Satan, with all power, signs," and so on (2 Thessalonians 2:9). In imitation of the bodily sojourn of Christ, of the dispensation for our sake, Satan comes and works in a man, as I have already said. This is what "with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one" means, as Isaiah says. For after mentioning the one from the root of Jesse, he added: "He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one" (Isaiah 11:4). And he foretold the striking of the earth also through the last of the prophets. For after saying: "A sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear me" (Malachi 4:2), and after a little: "Behold, I am sending you Elijah the Tishbite" (Malachi 4:5), he added as a final word: "lest I come and strike the earth utterly" (Malachi 4:6). "And he will abolish him by the appearing of his coming" (2 Thessalonians 2:8). The apostle called Christ our life, and he added: "When your life is revealed" (Colossians 3:4). Therefore when life is revealed from heaven, it is impossible that the one who procures death should not be abolished, whose coming is "according to the working of Satan" (2 Thessalonians 2:9). This ought to persuade the Apollinarians and the Arians that God the Word assumed a complete man. For in imitation of the righteousness and the dispensation for our sake, Satan comes and will work in a man.
notes: The source text contains a duplicated passage: the Isaiah quotation and the Malachi material appear twice, once in the main text and once in a parallel column (335,col2), with minor variations (e.g., τοῖς φοβουμένοις με vs. τοῖς φοβουμένοις; ἀποστελῶ vs. ἀποστέλλω; τελευταῖον ἐπήγαγεν λόγον vs. καὶ ἐπήγαγε). Both are glossed in order as they appear.
The lemma form παρουσίας appears in the source as παρουσίας in the phrase τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, but the glossary term is παρουσία; the lemma entry uses the dictionary form.
The text contains a page break marker 'παρουσ336 σία' and '336,ξολ2' indicating column breaks in the manuscript; these are not translated but noted for transparency.

last_rejected.quote: "A sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear me, and healing in its wings" (Malachi 4:2)
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀνατελεῖ ὑμῖν τοῖς φοβουμένοις με ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης
last_rejected.why: LXX Mal 4:2 has 'who fear my name', not 'who fear me'. The Greek says φοβουμένοις με, but the standard LXX text reads φοβουμένοις τὸ ὄνομά μου.
last_rejected.fix: "A sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear my name, and healing in its wings" (Malachi 4:2)
last_rejected.ruling: φοβουμένοις με in source matches 'who fear me'; translator accurately rendered what text says, not standard LXX.

last_rejected.source_quote: κατὰ μίμησιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ τῆς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν οἰκονομίας
last_rejected.why: Source says 'in imitation of the righteousness AND the dispensation,' but 'righteousness' here refers to Christ (the Sun of Righteousness just quoted). English 'righteousness' alone loses the christological reference.
last_rejected.fix: in imitation of the Sun of Righteousness and the dispensation for our sake
last_rejected.ruling: κατὰ μίμησιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης is correctly rendered 'in imitation of the righteousness'; no meaning is lost.

last_rejected.why: The English attributes 'as I have already said' to Severian's own voice, but in context this is the author speaking. Actually this seems correct—Severian is speaking. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: καθὼς καὶ ἤδη εἶπον correctly rendered; reporter agrees no error.

last_rejected.quote: A sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear me
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀνατελεῖ ὑμῖν τοῖς φοβουμένοις ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης / ἀνατελεῖ ὑμῖν τοῖς φοβουμένοις με ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης
last_rejected.why: Second occurrence has 'me' (φοβουμένοις με) = 'who fear ME,' omitted in English. This changes the scriptural quotation.
last_rejected.fix: A sun of righteousness will rise for you who fear me
last_rejected.ruling: Both occurrences translated identically; first source occurrence lacks 'με' so no omission in first instance.

last_rejected.quote: of necessity he also abolishes the devil
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐξ ἀνάγκης καταργεῖ καὶ τὸν τοῦ θανάτου πρόξενον τὸν διάβολον
last_rejected.why: Source has 'of necessity he abolishes ALSO the devil'—the 'also' (καί) is omitted in English, losing the connection that Christ abolishes both the man of lawlessness AND the devil.
last_rejected.fix: of necessity he also abolishes the devil
last_rejected.ruling: καί before τὸν τοῦ θανάτου πρόξενον is adequately captured by 'he also abolishes' in English.

last_rejected.quote: it is impossible that the one who procures death should not be abolished
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀδύνατον μὴ καταργηθῆναι τὸν τοῦ θανάτου πρόξενον
last_rejected.why: English adds 'should not be' making a double negative construction, but source says 'impossible not to be abolished' = 'impossible that he not be abolished.' The English 'should not be abolished' could be misread. Actually this is grammatically tricky but conveys the same meaning. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀδύνατον μὴ καταργηθῆναι correctly rendered as 'impossible that...should not be abolished'; same meaning.

last_rejected.quote: And he foretold that he would strike the earth also through the last of the prophets
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ δὲ πατάξειν αὐτὸν τὴν γῆν προεῖπε καὶ διὰ τοῦ ὑστέρου τῶν προφητῶν
last_rejected.why: First occurrence: 'that HE would strike'—the subject is Christ (the one from Jesse's root), but English 'he would strike' is ambiguous. Actually this is clear enough from context. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: πατάξειν αὐτόν rendered 'he would strike'; pronoun clear from context. No error per reporter.

last_rejected.quote: And he foretold the striking of the earth also through the last of the prophets
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ δὲ πατάσσειν τὴν γῆν προεῖπεν καὶ διὰ τοῦ ὑστέρου τῶν προφητῶν
last_rejected.why: Second occurrence changes from 'that he would strike' (πατάξειν) to 'the striking' (πατάσσειν), a different grammatical form. English correctly uses noun form 'striking.' No error.
last_rejected.ruling: πατάσσειν (noun-form infinitive) correctly rendered 'the striking'; reporter agrees no error.

last_rejected.quote: He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with breath through lips he will destroy the impious one
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ πατάξει τὴν γῆν τῷ λόγῳ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν πνεύματι διὰ χειλέων ἀνελεῖ τὸν ἀσεβῆ
last_rejected.why: English adds 'and' before 'with breath' not in source, and changes 'the impious one' (τὸν ἀσεβῆ) to 'the impious one'—correct. But 'impious one' for ἀσεβῆ is fine. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Minor conjunction 'and' reflects Greek καί before ἐν πνεύματι; ἀσεβῆ correctly 'impious one.'

last_rejected.why: Source has 'when YOUR life is revealed' (ὑμῶν), but earlier the source had 'our life' (ἡμῶν). English correctly tracks this shift. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑμῶν correctly 'your' vs ἡμῶν 'our'; reporter agrees no error.

last_rejected.quote: For in imitation of the righteousness and the dispensation for our sake, Satan comes and will work in a man
last_rejected.source_quote: κατὰ γὰρ μίμησιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ τῆς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν οἰκονομίας ἔρχεται ὁ σατανᾶς καὶ ἐνεργήσει ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ
last_rejected.why: As noted, 'righteousness' alone misses the christological reference to the Sun of Righteousness. This is a significant theological point in the argument.
last_rejected.fix: in imitation of the Sun of Righteousness and the dispensation for our sake
last_rejected.ruling: δικαιοσύνης correctly 'righteousness'; same as #1, no meaning lost in standard rendering.
